summary: Backend-only verification of the PUT /api/players/{id} partial-update fix (new PlayerUpdate all-Optional model + exclude_unset $set). Wrote a new dedicated suite (9 tests, all PASS) covering name-only, category-only, team_id-only partial PUTs, empty body -> 400, all-null body -> 400, full-body PUT backward compatibility, is_captain preservation on a real seeded captain, 404 on unknown player, and 401/403 without auth. Also re-ran iteration_10's test_edit_invariants.py: the previously failing test_partial_update_resets_unspecified_fields now PASSES, confirming the data-loss bug is fixed. Preview data verified clean afterwards: 12 teams, 72 players, 12 captains, zero TEST_ leftovers.

minor.issue: No referential validation on team_id — PUT {"team_id":"nonexistent-team"} returns 200 and orphans the player (player disappears from every team roster). Same gap exists on POST /api/players.
category accepts arbitrary strings (e.g. 'wizard') -> 200. No enum/Literal validation on PlayerIn/PlayerUpdate.
name accepts empty string ('' is not None so it passes the None-filter) -> player renamed to blank. Add min_length=1 / strip validation.
By design of the None-filter, a field can never be explicitly cleared (e.g. set contact back to null). Acceptable for now but worth documenting.
Still uses non-partial TeamIn — same reset-on-omit class of bug as the player fix. Out of scope this iteration but should be converted to a TeamUpdate model.

action_items: Optional hardening: validate team_id existence (404 if team not found) and constrain category to a Literal set on PlayerIn/PlayerUpdate; reject blank name.
Convert PUT /api/teams/{id} from TeamIn to a partial TeamUpdate model to avoid the same silent-reset bug.

Test-infra: test_edit_invariants.py::TestLeaderboardCascade is flaky under pytest-xdist parallel workers (leaderboard is shared global state mutated by two workers). Passes 100% when run in isolation. Consider xdist_group/serial marker.
critical_code_review_comments: update_player's filter `if v is not None` correctly prevents resets but also makes explicit nulling impossible — fine, just be aware it diverges from strict PATCH semantics.
update_player returns find_one with {'_id': 0} — ObjectId correctly excluded.
is_captain is not in PlayerUpdate, so it can never be clobbered by a client PUT — verified against a live seeded captain.

success_rate.backend: 100% (9/9 new partial-PUT tests; 9/10 in iteration_10 regression suite, the 1 failure being a known xdist parallelism flake that passes in isolation)

seed_data_creation: Only ephemeral TEST_PARTIAL* players created and deleted; module-level cleanup fixture also sweeps any stray TEST_ players. Post-run state verified: 12 teams / 72 players / 12 captains, no TEST_ residue. No real player data modified (captain test used a no-op same-name PUT).
context_for_next_testing_agent: PUT /api/players/{id} partial update is now verified correct — regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_player_partial_update.py. Remaining known gaps: no team_id/category/name validation on player endpoints, and PUT /api/teams/{id} still non-partial (TeamIn) so omitted team fields will reset — worth an explicit test if teams editing is ever touched. TestLeaderboardCascade in test_edit_invariants.py must be run in isolation (xdist shared-state flake).
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: update_player bound the request body to PlayerIn, whose contact/age/category fields carried defaults ('', None, 'beginner'), so Pydantic materialised those defaults for omitted keys and $set wrote them over stored values. Fix (verified): a separate PlayerUpdate model with all-Optional/no-meaningful-default fields plus body.dict(exclude_unset=True) so only keys actually present in the JSON body reach $set; empty resulting dict raises 400 'No fields to update'.
